system.name: Graph-Based Oracle Construction
system.one_liner: an approach that builds statement-dependency graphs from transaction executions to construct semantically-equivalent test-case oracles for detecting transactional bugs in DBMSs

components.name: Databases
components.role: the DBMSs under test that random SQL statements are generated against

components.name: SQL statements for each transaction
components.role: randomly generated SQL statements composing each transaction

components.name: Item-tracking instrumentation
components.role: instruments SQL statements to track item-level accesses

components.name: Version-set-tracking instrumentation
components.role: instruments SQL statements to track version-set accesses

components.name: Instrumented test case
components.role: the SQL test case after instrumentation, ready for execution

components.name: Transaction Execution
components.role: executes the instrumented transactions (Txn 0, Txn 1, Txn 2) against a database

components.name: Statement output
components.role: recorded output of each statement captured during transaction execution

components.name: Statement-dependency graph
components.role: graph describing the dependencies among statements in the transactions

components.name: Graph Decycling
components.role: removes cycles from the statement-dependency graph, rebuilding or refining and re-executing the test case as needed

components.name: Acyclic graph
components.role: the cycle-free statement-dependency graph produced by Graph Decycling

components.name: Semantically Equivalent Test Case
components.role: SQL test case built by topologically sorting the acyclic graph so statements run in dependency order without transactions

components.name: Execution without transactions
components.role: runs the semantically-equivalent test case's statements individually, outside of transactions

components.name: Refined test case
components.role: a refined test case fed back for re-execution when the graph must be rebuilt

components.name: Transaction execution results
components.role: results of the original transaction execution used as the comparison baseline

components.name: Execution results comparison
components.role: compares the equivalent test case's results against the original transaction execution results

components.name: Equivalent
components.role: outcome when both executions produce the same results, i.e. no bug detected

components.name: Not equivalent
components.role: outcome when results differ, indicating a detected transactional bug

content.key_idea: By recording how statements in real transaction executions depend on each other, the approach builds a dependency graph and reorders it into an equivalent transaction-free test case, then treats disagreement between the two executions as evidence of a transactional bug.
content.reading_order: Left to right across the three numbered steps at top (Random Generation, SQL-level Instrumentation, Building Statement-Dependency Graph), then down into the large Transactional Oracle Construction box (step 4) ending at the Equivalent/Not equivalent verdict.

summary: This figure gives an overview of a graph-based approach for detecting transactional bugs in database engines. Random SQL statements are generated for each transaction against target Databases (step 1), instrumented for item- and version-set-tracking (step 2), and executed so their per-statement outputs can be recorded and built into a statement-dependency graph (step 3). In the larger Transactional Oracle Construction stage (step 4), Graph Decycling removes cycles from this graph, optionally refining and re-executing the test case; the resulting acyclic graph is topologically sorted into a Semantically Equivalent Test Case whose statements are executed individually, without transactions. Comparing these results against the original Transaction execution results yields an Equivalent or Not equivalent verdict, with the latter flagging a bug. The figure is a numbered pipeline of gray process and container boxes with a highlighted comparison step at the end.
